page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz with two threads per core. The processor incorporates a 260 MB Level 3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is 128 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage and no dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate competitive throughput in memory-bound and compute workloads. In large-block memory tests, the instance registers strong throughput with 216.15 GB/sec for uncached reads and 92.55 GB/sec for writes. Single-core performance is robust, producing a Geekbench single-core score of 1971.0 and solid physics processing capabilities. For specialized compute tasks, AMX and vector extensions aid small and medium model LLM inference, achieving 403.9 tokens/sec during text generation on a 135M model and 200.4 tokens/sec during prompt processing on a 7B model. Static web serving throughput reaches 56.39 GB/sec, while general multi-core compute tests such as Stress-NG and Clang compilation fall within median expectations.

The absence of local ephemeral storage necessitates remote storage provisioning for all operational persistence, which dictates IOPS and throughput caps based on external disk selection. However, the balance of 32 vCPUs, 128 GB of memory, and dedicated Intel Xeon hardware delivers consistent CPU execution without hypervisor oversubscription. This instance profile is well suited for enterprise application hosting, relational databases, static web serving, containerized services, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D32s_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 16-core, 32-thread Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked up to 4.2 GHz, paired with 128 GB of system memory. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V with an x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX along with AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local disk storage or discrete GPUs, requiring external Premium Storage for all persistent volumes. Synthetic benchmarks highlight strong uncached memory bandwidth of 216.15 GB/sec, high static web serving throughput at 56.39 GB/sec, and fast text generation on small LLM architectures. Offering a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio without core oversubscription, the D32s_v6 is geared toward enterprise application servers, memory-intensive web workloads, relational databases, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
